subject.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths

question: Should OpenClaw treat clean empty assistant replies from all cron executions as silent success by default, including delivered announce/webhook cron jobs, or should the fix be narrowed to no-delivery/per-job opt-in behavior?
rationale: The code change is mechanically small and proven, but it changes user-visible cron status and delivery semantics for existing jobs, which automation cannot decide safely without maintainer product intent.

options.title: Accept all-cron silent success
options.body: Merge this executor-boundary approach as the canonical fix for the reported regression, accepting that empty cron output means nothing to deliver unless another failure path fires.

options.title: Narrow before merge
options.body: Ask for the flag to be gated to `delivery.mode: "none"` or another existing silent-delivery signal to preserve empty-response failures for delivered jobs.

options.title: Pause for a public config contract
options.body: Hold this PR and design a per-job silent-empty option before changing default cron behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept all-cron silent success
recommendation.body: Merge this executor-boundary approach as the canonical fix for the reported regression, accepting that empty cron output means nothing to deliver unless another failure path fires.

likelyOwner.reason: The likely decision owner has recent history in both cron executor behavior and embedded terminal-state policy, which are the two affected decision surfaces.
